Apple is expected to announce the iPhone 18 series this September as usual, but this year's launch will echo several aspects of the unique circumstances surrounding the iPhone release during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic.

How this fall's iPhone announcement will differ from Apple's usual approach

Apple has many hugely successful products, but the iPhone has always been its crown jewel, accounting for a large share of the company's overall revenue.

So it's no surprise that Apple strives to maintain consistency with its iPhone launches. By keeping to a predictable new iPhone release schedule, Apple can better keep both Wall Street and its customers happy.

Generally, Apple unveils the new iPhone in early September—usually four new models—and has them all shipping by late September.

But 2020 was an unusual year because of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The 2020 fall iPhone lineup wasn't announced until October, and only two of the new models shipped initially, with the other two delayed until November.

This year, rumors suggest we'll see a similar kind of disruption to Apple's launch plans.

While a September announcement is still expected, Apple may not ship all of the new iPhone models at the same time.

As in 2020, only two models are likely to be available for purchase at first: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The much-anticipated foldable iPhone Ultra is expected to make its debut in September, but rumors suggest its release date may be pushed back slightly, potentially arriving a few weeks after the Pro models.

Apple may also differ from its usual approach when it comes to the total number of new iPhone models.

If rumors are true that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 will be delayed until spring 2027, then only three new models will debut this fall—the smallest fall iPhone lineup since 2019.

Whether driven by strategic considerations, the challenges posed by the global memory crisis, or the difficulties of mass-producing an entirely new foldable device, Apple's fall 2026 announcement could mirror several aspects of 2020.

What would you like to see Apple bring to this fall's iPhone event? Let us know in the comments.
